# kaf-mirror

> kaf-mirror mirrors topics between any two Kafka clusters over the Kafka protocol. It has a web dashboard, a management CLI, an audit trail and compliance reports. Apache Kafka, Confluent, Redpanda and Azure Event Hubs can be the source or the target, and KafScale is a supported target. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and written in Go.

What it does:

- A job consumes from a source cluster and produces to a target cluster. Topic names are kept by default. Exact and regex mappings are optional.
- Source offsets are committed only after the target acknowledges the write.
- TLS, mTLS, SASL PLAIN, SCRAM and Kerberos are supported.
- Access is role based: admin, operator, monitoring and compliance.
- Job metrics, lag, an audit trail and scheduled compliance reports are built in.
- It runs as one binary, in Docker, or in Kubernetes with the Helm chart.

What it is not:

- It is not tied to KafScale. KafScale is one supported target, useful when you want a backup on S3 that a bad delete on the source does not reach.
- A replica copies deletes and bad writes. For a backup, use a separate target with separate credentials.

## Start here

- [Get started]({{SITE}}start.html): run it with Docker or Helm.
- [Demo video]({{SITE}}media/demo.mp4): two Kafka clusters, one job, about two minutes.
- [Documentation index]({{SITE}}docs.html): configuration, RBAC, protection and API docs.
- [CLI reference]({{SITE}}cli-commands.html): every mirror-cli and admin-cli command.
